key_insight: LLMs showed improving but incomplete ACEP guideline concordance, with the best configuration scoring 98.6% and no consistent benefit from added reasoning.
clinical_relevance: EM-BENCH offers a reproducible way to assess guideline application in emergency medicine, without establishing safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: 210 physician-validated, binary vignettes spanning 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies.
149 configurations representing 79 base models evaluated using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring.
Accuracy compared by access tier, model size, release date, policy, evidence level, and reasoning settings.
evidence_signal: The top configuration answered 207/210 correctly; median accuracy was 91% for closed-access versus 63% for open-weight models.
watch_item: Performance on binary guideline vignettes may not generalize to complex clinical workflows or patient outcomes.
paper_title: EM-BENCH: A Reproducible Framework for Benchmarking Guideline-Concordant Clinical Decision Making in Large Language Models
